name: Mozambique
headline: Mozambique: −0.2% growth in 2025, 4.4% inflation, debt 90% of GDP
sections: Mozambique is a $23.6 billion economy (2025), the world's 128th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew −0.2% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $1,698 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 6.2% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.4% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 10.4% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 6.6% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 11.6% (2025).
Gross government debt is 90% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 120% in 2020. The general government balance is −5.1% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −13.5% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 97% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 25.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 99% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 63.8 years (2024). Population: 35.8 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
